heading: Your Questions About Orthodontic Care at Chang Orthodontics, Answered
subheading: From your first appointment in Los Alamitos to the day your braces come off, here's what you need to know.

items.q: Do I need a referral to schedule a consultation with Dr. Chang?
items.a: No referral is needed — you can contact Chang Orthodontics directly at (562) 430-0541 to schedule your complimentary consultation. Dr. Chang welcomes patients of all ages from Los Alamitos and the surrounding communities. Simply call or reach out online and our team will find a convenient time for you.

items.q: What should I do if I have an orthodontic emergency, like a broken wire or loose bracket?
items.a: Chang Orthodontics provides emergency care for issues like broken wires, loose brackets, or discomfort that can't wait for a routine visit. Call us at (562) 430-0541 as soon as possible so we can assess the situation and get you seen quickly. In the meantime, if a wire is poking, you can use orthodontic wax to cover the sharp area for temporary relief.

items.q: Does Chang Orthodontics accept dental insurance or offer payment plans?
items.a: We work with many dental insurance plans and will help you understand and maximize your orthodontic benefits. For patients without insurance or with remaining out-of-pocket costs, flexible payment options are available to make treatment more accessible. We encourage you to call our Los Alamitos office at (562) 430-0541 to discuss your specific coverage and financing needs.

items.q: What happens during my first visit to Chang Orthodontics?
items.a: Your initial consultation gives Dr. Chang the opportunity to evaluate your teeth, jaw, and overall bite using modern diagnostic tools, including digital X-rays that emit significantly less radiation than traditional X-rays. Dr. Chang will discuss any concerns, explain your treatment options, and outline a personalized plan that fits your goals and lifestyle. You'll also have the chance to ask questions and learn about estimated timelines and costs before committing to anything.

items.q: At what age should my child have their first orthodontic evaluation?
items.a: The American Association of Orthodontists recommends that children have their first orthodontic screening around age 7. Dr. Chang offers early orthodontic treatment — sometimes called Phase 1 treatment — to address developing issues while a child's jaw and facial bones are still growing, which can simplify or even eliminate the need for more extensive treatment later. Catching problems early through dentofacial orthopedics can guide proper jaw development and create space for incoming permanent teeth.

items.q: What is the Damon Smile system, and how is it different from traditional braces?
items.a: The Damon Smile system uses self-ligating brackets — meaning no elastic ties — which allows the wire to move more freely and reduces friction during tooth movement. Many patients find Damon braces more comfortable, easier to keep clean, and associated with fewer required adjustments compared to conventional braces. Dr. Chang can evaluate whether the Damon Smile system is a good fit for your specific case during your consultation.

items.q: Does Dr. Chang treat complex conditions like cleft lip and palate or craniofacial differences?
items.a: Yes — Dr. Chang has specialized training in craniofacial orthodontics, including treatment for patients with cleft lip and palate and other craniofacial conditions. These cases often require close coordination with oral surgeons, speech therapists, and other specialists, and Dr. Chang is experienced in managing that collaborative care. Families in the Los Alamitos area seeking this level of specialized orthodontic expertise are welcome to call (562) 430-0541 to discuss their child's needs.

items.q: How do I take care of my teeth after braces are removed?
items.a: Once your braces come off, Dr. Chang will fit you with a retainer to keep your teeth in their new positions — wearing it as directed is the most important step in maintaining your results. You'll have follow-up visits so Dr. Chang can monitor your bite and ensure your retainer still fits properly over time. Consistent retainer wear, along with regular dental cleanings, helps protect the investment you've made in your smile.
